subject: Capacity plan & unit-econ targets for ACMEHealth (post-demo)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + missing sizing info (ACMEHealth demo today)

Jordan — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and open items so we can get to a concrete reserved capacity plan: 

Summary from call:
- Target workload: patient note summarization + QA reranking for clinical search. Mostly streaming outputs; average response ~700–900 tokens.
- Peak concurrency observed in pilot: ~90 reqs/s (spiky around end of day windows). Steady-state expected ~35–45 reqs/s.
- Latency target: p95 < 450ms for standard summaries; 90% of traffic can tolerate up to 800ms.
- Data residency: US region, eventual VPC/private deployment considered.

Open items we need to finalize pricing and sizing:
1) Confirm monthly token volume (avg tokens/call * daily calls * working days). Your rough pilot projection was 150–250M tokens/month — can you confirm a tighter range?
2) Budget band for reserved capacity (monthly commit or yearly) — you mentioned an internal target of <$20k/month for committed throughput; is that still directionally correct?
3) Preferred GPU family (if you have procurement constraints): H100 versus A100 availability matters for lead time and pricing.

Attached: an initial capacity worksheet (acme_health_capacity_plan.xlsx) and a short throughput benchmark summary we ran on a comparable model (throughput_benchmarks.pdf).

Next steps: If you can reply with confirmed token range and any procurement constraints by EOD Thursday, Laura and I will run three sizing + $/1M token scenarios (cost-conservative, balanced, aggressive) and propose a canary reservation plus burst plan.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + missing sizing info (ACMEHealth demo today)

Thanks Ben — and thanks for the write-up. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token volume: our internal analytics team tightened projections this morning. Expect a baseline of ~180M tokens/month with a high-growth scenario up to ~320M tokens/month if adoption of the summary feature accelerates after rollout. Call-level average = 800 tokens (we measured median ~760, mean ~810).
- Concurrency/throughput: confirmed pilot peak at 95 reqs/s but plan to architect for 120 reqs/s headroom. Steady state estimate 40–50 reqs/s. Burst tolerance is important for end-of-day batch processing windows.
- Budget: procurement asked for a committed band that targets cost at or below $20k/month initially. We can stretch to $28k/month if the unit economics reach <$22 per 1M tokens for the committed tier.
- GPU preference: Procurement prefers H100 if lead times are reasonable; A100 is acceptable as backup. We also flagged that we need a distinction between dedicated reserve and burstable access for short high-volume windows.

Attaching a short procurement note (sent separately).

Jordan Ellis
Senior PM, Clinical Applications
ACMEHealth
j.ellis@acmehealth.com
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: sizing + $/1M targets for ACMEHealth (action items)

Ben/Laura — looping in Neha for SRE/benchmark input. Jordan's reply gives us: baseline 180M tokens/mo, upside 320M, avg ~800 tokens/call, target headroom 120 reqs/s, procurement target <$20k/mo but can go to $28k/mo if unit-econ < $22/1M tokens.

Actionable asks (please reply inline):
- Laura: produce three draft reserved plans (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive). Include: GPU type (H100 vs A100), number of GPUs in reserved pool, expected average tokens/minute and p95 latency estimates. For each plan show assumed utilization and resulting $/1M tokens (include both hosted and reserved blended unit-econ if they will use burst).
- Neha: run quick back-of-envelope on throughput per GPU for our recommended model at 800 tokens avg (use existing bench reports). Provide expected reqs/s per GPU for H100 and A100 and the expected KV-cache savings for prefix reuse in this workflow.
- Ben: confirm with Jordan whether they prefer a monthly commit or 12-month reserved pricing; also confirm whether they need VPC/private on day-1 or later. Procurement often pushes for annual to get better unit pricing.

We have 24 hours to get a coherent commercial alternative back to Jordan. Laura — flag anything that needs legal (pricing floors, SLAs) and I will triage.

Evelyn
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: three reserve options + unit-econ (ACMEHealth)

Jordan — thanks for the fast follow. Per the internal runbook we sent three concise options below (high-level, attachment contains the detailed workbook):

Attachments: acme_health_capacity_plan.xlsx (detailed breakdown), throughput_benchmarks.pdf

Option A — Conservative (lower commit, burst support)
- Reserved: 2 x A100 (40GB) GPUs in a dedicated pool.
- Expected steady throughput: ~65 reqs/s reserved; burst up to 120 reqs/s via on-demand shared fleet.
- Assumed utilization: 55% steady; effective blended $/1M tokens: $27.5 (monthly billing).
- Notes: Meets p95 latency target for standard summaries; lower upfront cost and faster provisioning.

Option B — Balanced (recommended)
- Reserved: 2 x H100 (80GB) GPUs + 1x burstable slot (shared).
- Expected steady throughput: ~95 reqs/s reserved; handles 120 reqs/s baseline with short bursts.
- Assumed utilization: 70%. Effective $/1M tokens: $20.8 (monthly commit).
- Notes: Best balance of latency and unit economics; aligns with procurement's sweet spot if they commit monthly at $21–22/1M.

Option C — Aggressive (cost-optimized for high volume)
- Reserved: 4 x H100 (80GB) GPUs in pool.
- Expected steady throughput: ~200 reqs/s; comfortably covers 320M tokens/month upside.
- Assumed utilization: 75–80%. Effective $/1M tokens: $14.9 (annual committed pricing).
- Notes: Requires annual commitment to achieve the low unit price and longer procurement lead time.

Quick notes on assumptions (see attachment for full modeled math):
- Average tokens/call = 800 (per Jordan).
- We factor KV-cache savings for repeated prefixes ~10% token reduction in served cost for this workflow.
- Blended unit-econ assumes 10% of traffic served via burst (on-demand) in Conservative/Balanced plans.

Requested next steps:
1) Can Procurement confirm preference: Monthly commit vs 12-month reserved? (Jordan / procurement@acmehealth.com)
2) If Procurement prefers monthly, Option B gets us closest to your <$22/1M target at ~ $21/1M with a 2xH100+burst config.
3) If you want us to prepare a formal quote + SOW for legal review, we'll include a canary rollout plan and SLA targets; give us target signature date and we'll schedule internal pricing approvals.

If this aligns, I'll push a formal quote (DocuSign) and a timeline for provisioning (H100 lead time ~3–5 weeks from PO; A100 typically 1–2 weeks).

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: acme_health_capacity_plan.xlsx (workbook), throughput_benchmarks.pdf
